q: The class of computable dynamical systems (Julia sets, Newton's method dynamics) and their decidability: for a given polynomial p(z), the problem 'does the Newton iteration starting at z₀ converge to a root?' is:
opts: Computable for almost all z₀ but undecidable on the Julia set (boundary between basins)
exp: Newton's method convergence is computable for points away from the Julia set (finite escape time or convergence within a basin). On the Julia set itself, the boundary between basins, convergence is not computable in general—this is a manifestation of the Blum-Shub-Smale (BSS) undecidability.
